messages.subject: Binary outcome continuous mediator question
parts:
I'm doing a simple mediation that has a binary y, a continuous m and binary x.

I'm wondering if I can get standardized coefficients in laavan, and how to get total, direct, and indirect effects.  I can't seem to get the indirect and direct effects to print either, but that may be because I'm coming back to r after some time away.  

Current code.
# simple mediation 
simpmed <- 'qa ~ c*group + b*totsi
totsi ~ a*group
naive.indirect := a*b
naive.direct := c'

fit <- sem(simpmed, data=rdata,
           ordered=c("qa","group"))
summary(fit)


medeff<- '
qa ~ c*group + b*totsi
totsi ~ a*group
# label threshold for qa
qa | b0*t1
probit11 := (-b0+c+b*a)/sqrt(bˆ2+1)
probit10 := (-b0+c )/sqrt(bˆ2+1)
probit00 := (-b0 )/sqrt(bˆ2+1)
indirect := pnorm(probit11) - pnorm(probit10)
direct := pnorm(probit10) - pnorm(probit00)
OR.indirect := (pnorm(probit11)/(1-pnorm(probit11)))/
  (pnorm(probit10)/(1-pnorm(probit10)))
OR.direct := (pnorm(probit10)/(1-pnorm(probit10)))/
  (pnorm(probit00)/(1-pnorm(probit00)))
'

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Binary outcome continuous mediator question
parts: I'm doing a simple mediation that has a binary y, a continuous m and binary x.  I'm wondering if I can get standardized coefficients in laavan

You can request standardized parameters with summary(fit, standardized = TRUE).  But I'm not sure what the behavior is or what would make sense.  It doesn't make sense to think of a 1-SD change in a binary X, so I would not want the slope to be standardized in terms of the predictor, just the continuous mediator.
